title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. C is a category, almost certainly abelian (the first line reads 'C cat. abélienne'). S is a commutative Z-graded ring concentrated in degrees >= 0. M = M(C,S) is the category of graded S-module objects in C, i.e. graded objects (M_i) of C with an action of S. M_N and M^N are full subcategories 'defined as above', presumably modules concentrated in degrees <= N (resp. >= N).

Step 1 (truncation). The inclusion i_N : M_N -> M has an adjoint tau_N : M -> M_N, with a natural map P -> i_N tau_N(P). This is the truncation P -> P/P_{>N}, which is surjective. So tau_N is really the LEFT adjoint of i_N, i.e. i_N admits a left adjoint. The manuscript's 'à droite' is ambiguous or loosely worded.

Step 2 (adjoint of truncation). Grothendieck asks for a right adjoint phi_N of tau_N:
  Hom_{M_N}(tau_N P, Q) = Hom_M(P, phi_N Q), for Q in M_N.
Such a phi_N exists iff, for fixed Q, the functor P |-> Hom(tau_N P, Q) is representable. Since tau_N is a left adjoint, it commutes with colimits. Hence this functor turns colimits into limits. By an adjoint-functor-theorem argument this suffices when C or C° is a 'catégorie de modèles' (in modern terms: locally presentable, or Grothendieck with a generator).

Step 3 (explicit components). For any M one has M_i = Hom*(S, M)_i = Hom*(S[-i], M)_0, where Hom* is the internal graded Hom with values in C. Applying the adjunction internally (marked 'justifier'), and using tau_N(S[-i]) = (tau_{N-i} S)[-i]:
  (phi_N Q)_i = Hom*(tau_N(S[-i]), Q)_0 = Hom*((tau_{N-i} S)[-i], Q)_0.
So phi_N Q is a 'coinduced' module. Degreewise it is Hom_S(S/S_{>N-i}, Q) with a shift.

What it serves. When S is a polynomial (symmetric) algebra, the graded duals of the truncations S/S_{>k} are truncated divided-power algebras. So this right adjoint is the formal mechanism by which divided-power objects appear as adjoints or duals to truncation. That fits the folder's theme (divided-power de Rham complex, 1976 IHÉS lecture).

Physical context. The sheet is the verso of a typescript page of SGA 7, Exp. IX ('Définition de l'accouplement de monodromie', p. 100, §9.1). The typed text visible through the paper and the next page's transcription are from that typescript. The previous page is likewise the back of an unrelated MP exam problem.
errors: Direction of adjunction: the text says i_N 'admet foncteur adjoint à droite' tau_N, but the natural map P -> i_N tau_N P (the unit) shows tau_N is the left adjoint of i_N. Either a slip or the phrase means 'i_N is right adjoint'.
The representability argument needs a set-theoretic or solution-set hypothesis. Grothendieck acknowledges this ('lorsque C ou C° est une cat. de modèles'), so it is a gap only in general.

The step Hom*(S[-i], phi_N Q)_0 = Hom*(tau_N(S[-i]), Q)_0 uses an internal (C-valued) version of the adjunction, which is not automatic from the set-valued one. The margin note 'justifier' flags exactly this. It holds since tau_N is compatible with tensoring by objects of C / Z-modules, but this needs checking.

ideas.what: Truncation functor tau_N left adjoint to the inclusion of graded modules concentrated in degrees <= N
Right adjoint phi_N of truncation, existence via colimit preservation plus representability for 'categories of models'
ideas.modern_name: special/Freyd adjoint functor theorem for locally presentable categories; coinduction

ideas.what: Explicit formula (phi_N Q)_i = Hom*((tau_{N-i}S)[-i], Q)_0, a coinduced module whose components are Homs out of truncated S; for S symmetric this produces divided-power duals
ideas.modern_name: coinduced module / graded dual of truncated symmetric algebra = truncated divided powers
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (divided powers as graded dual of Sym: Cartan, Roby)

missed.claim: Archival detail: these divided-power de Rham notes (c. 1975-76) are written on the versos of SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript pages (monodromy pairing, §9.1).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Helps date and order the sheets and the SGA 7 typescript drafts; no mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine categorical construction: a right adjoint to truncation of graded modules with an explicit coinduced formula. Standard material, plausibly a lemma toward divided-power duality; nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'C cat. abélienne'.
The arrow is P -> i_N tau_N(P) (unit map, probably surjective), not an inclusion.
'il est représent.' likely 'il est adjoint' or refers to tau_N being a left adjoint; the argument is that tau_N commutes with lim->.
The superscript annotation near Hom_{M_N}(tau_N P, Q) is 'Q ∈ M_N' rather than an overset cap.
Final line: '= (Hom*((tau_{N-i}(S))[-i], Q) ...)_0' with a scribbled-out fragment; the earlier line has 'justifier' as a margin note.
